Resolves #18868

`check-consumer-runtime-build` now also compiles the App worker from the installed copy, so a specifier that resolves only while this repository is the root fails the check wherever it sits in a shipped app. It compiles `webpack.config.appworker.mjs` as the framework, standing in the consumer. In consumer mode that config moves the app context to the workspace root. There, webpack's context walk rewrites every `./node_modules/…` file to a bare request, which the context's `^\.\/` regExp drops, so it reaches no shipped app. As the framework it reaches all 153.

Evidence: **L3** — a real `npm pack` → install → App-worker compile, red with one of PR #18851's specifiers reverted and green restored. This PR's own `guard` job is the same run on a GitHub runner.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline jobs ran. Change class: `capability` (`feat`).

## Deltas from ticket

- **The premise was half right, and the ticket body is corrected.** A consumer in consumer mode never compiles the engine's apps. The Institution compiled them because its `build-all` runs `all.mjs -f -n`, which is framework mode. create-app's template runs `all.mjs -n`. The check uses framework mode as the one instrument that compiles every shipped app from an installed copy. It does not endorse `-f` for consumers; I asked @neo-fable-clio whether the Institution means it.
- **The fixture grows by what the App config needs:** `acorn` and `astring` for the template loader, and the `src/MicroLoader.mjs` the config copies from every workspace.
- **The path filter is now a rule:** every tree an installed copy compiles, plus `buildScripts/**`, instead of 12 named files.
- **One mode for the App worker (development):** a specifier that resolves nowhere fails both modes.

## Test Evidence

- **Red first:** the AC-2 run above, on the check's own instrument.
- **Local:** the full check 25 s on an M-series Mac (16 s before the App arm).
- **Unit:** `unit/buildScripts/checkConsumerRuntimeBuild.spec.mjs` 11/11. Two arms are new: an App graph holding the view and the bundle passes, and one that reached no shipped app fails twice.
- The `lint-staged` guards were run by hand (hooks do not run in a worktree), and all exit 0.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: No build guide records how far the App worker's context reaches in each build mode. Consumer mode rewrites `./node_modules/…` to bare requests the `^\.\/` regExp drops, so it reaches no shipped app. Framework mode (`-f`) reaches every one. #18868 first assumed the opposite and was corrected by measurement. The fact now lives only in this check's docblock.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: N/A
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: An error list proves nothing about a compile that reached no modules. `APP_EXPECTATIONS` is what makes "no errors" mean "every shipped app resolved". The unit arm *an App compile that reached no shipped app fails, however clean its error list* pins that direction.
